n: Even a powerful king’s heart is in God’s hand, as easily directed as a farmer channels irrigation water. No ruler is beyond God’s reach.

f.g: Irrigation channels that a farmer opens or closes to guide water.

n: People think their ways are right, but the Lord weighs hearts. (Compare 16:2.)
Doing what is right and just pleases the Lord more than sacrifice. Ritual cannot replace righteous living—a theme the prophets repeat.

f.w: more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice

n: Haughty eyes and a proud heart—the very “lamp” that guides the wicked—are sin.

f.g: Hebrew can be read “the lamp of the wicked”—what guides their life.

n: Careful planning by diligent people leads to profit; hasty shortcuts lead to poverty.
A fortune made by lying is a vanishing mist and a deadly trap.

f.w: a vanity tossed to and fro

n: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is right.

f.g: Literally “drag them away,” as in a net.

n: The path of the guilty is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
Better to live in a cramped corner of the roof than share a big house with a quarrelsome spouse. Flat roofs in Israel could hold a small room or shelter.

f.g: Flat roofs were living space; a corner offered little room or shelter.

n: The wicked crave evil; they show no mercy even to their neighbors.

f.w: findeth no favour in his eyes

n: When a mocker is punished, the naive learn; when the wise are taught, they grow in knowledge.
The Righteous One—likely God—observes the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.

f.g: Possibly “the Righteous One,” a title for God.

n: Whoever ignores the cries of the poor will one day cry out and not be answered.

f.w: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor

n: A secret gift calms anger, and a bribe hidden in a cloak soothes fury. An observation of how things work, not an endorsement of bribery.

f.g: A gift slipped secretly into the fold of a garment.

n: Justice brings joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.

f.w: It is joy to the just to do judgment

n: Whoever strays from the path of wisdom ends up resting among the dead.

f.g: The assembly of the rephaim—the shades of the dead.

n: Whoever loves pleasure and luxury (wine and perfumed oil) will end up poor.
The wicked become the ransom for the righteous: trouble meant for the good falls on the wicked instead.
Better to live alone in the desert than with a contentious, angry spouse.
The wise have precious stores and oil in their homes, but fools gulp down all they have.

f.g: Swallows it all, uses it up.

n: Whoever pursues righteousness and loyal love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
Wisdom is stronger than military power: a wise person can capture a city of warriors and tear down the stronghold they trusted.

f.w: scaleth the city of the mighty

n: Guarding your mouth and tongue keeps you out of trouble.
The proud and arrogant person’s name is “Mocker”—he acts with insolent pride.
The lazy person’s cravings will kill him, because his hands refuse to work.

f.w: The desire of the slothful killeth him

n: The lazy covet all day long, but the righteous give without holding back.

f.w: the righteous giveth and spareth not

n: God detests the sacrifice of the wicked—even more when it’s offered with evil intent, like buying off God.

f.w: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination

n: A false witness will be destroyed, but a person who listens carefully will speak with lasting credibility.
The wicked put up a bold, brazen front, but the upright think carefully about their path.
No human wisdom, insight, or plan can succeed against the Lord.

f.w: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD

n: You can prepare horses for battle, but victory comes from the Lord. Prepare diligently—then trust God for the outcome.
